title: Benjamin Addresses the People
summary: King Benjamin calls his brethren’s attention and says he has more to tell them about what is to come.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin addresses his brethren and says he has more to tell them about what is to come.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Benjamin is visibly addressing an audience.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience’s appearance and size; the setting’s specific features.

spoken_dialogue.text: I would call your attention, for I have somewhat more to speak unto you;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict future events described in the address as happening in the present.

title: The Angel Appears to Benjamin
summary: Benjamin says an angel from God made these things known to him; in the account, the angel stood before him after he awoke.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin says the things he will tell the people were made known to him by an angel from God.
Benjamin says he awoke and saw the angel standing before him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel is standing before Benjamin in the remembered encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel’s appearance, clothing, and the precise setting of the encounter.

narration.text: And he said unto me: Awake; and I awoke,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The angel’s appearance is not described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific angelic form or add details to the remembered encounter.

title: Glad Tidings of Great Joy
summary: The angel tells Benjamin to awake and hear, declaring glad tidings of great joy and saying the Lord has heard Benjamin’s prayers and sent the angel so Benjamin and his people may rejoice.

explicit_facts.text: The angel tells Benjamin to awake and hear the words the angel will tell him.
The angel says he came to declare glad tidings of great joy.
The angel says the Lord heard Benjamin’s prayers, judged his righteousness, and sent the angel so Benjamin and his people may rejoice.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel speaks to Benjamin in the remembered encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel’s appearance and the surroundings.

spoken_dialogue.text: Awake, and hear the words which I shall tell thee;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: an angel from God

spoken_dialogue.text: I am come to declare unto you the glad tidings of great joy.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: an angel from God

prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the future events the angel will describe as occurring in this scene.

title: The Coming of the Lord Omnipotent
summary: The Lord Omnipotent is foretold to come down from heaven among the children of men, dwell in a tabernacle of clay, work mighty miracles, and cast out devils or evil spirits.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord Omnipotent shall come down from heaven among the children of men and dwell in a tabernacle of clay.
He shall work mighty miracles, including healing the sick, raising the dead, causing the lame to walk, restoring sight and hearing, and curing diseases.
He shall cast out devils or evil spirits dwelling in the hearts of the children of men.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophecy can be presented as text without depicting its foretold events as presently occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker, audience, and present setting are not identified in these verses.
No physical appearance is specified for the Lord Omnipotent or the evil spirits.

narration.text: shall come down from heaven among the children of men, and shall dwell in a tabernacle of clay,
working mighty miracles, such as healing the sick, raising the dead,
And he shall cast out devils, or the evil spirits which dwell in the hearts of the children of men.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses describe future acts, not events occurring in a stated present setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify a speaker or audience from these verses.
Do not stage the foretold acts as present events or give the evil spirits a visible form.

title: Foretold Suffering and Name
summary: He shall suffer temptations, bodily pain, hunger, thirst, fatigue, and anguish. He shall be called Jesus Christ, and his mother shall be called Mary.

explicit_facts.text: He shall suffer temptations, bodily pain, hunger, thirst, and fatigue.
Blood shall come from every pore because of his anguish for the wickedness and abominations of his people.
He shall be called Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Father of heaven and earth, and the Creator of all things from the beginning.
His mother shall be called Mary.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophecy can be presented as text without depicting its foretold events as happening now.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and speaker are not identified in the supplied verses.
The appearances of Jesus Christ and Mary are not described.

narration.text: And lo, he shall suffer temptations, and pain of body, hunger, thirst, and fatigue,
so great shall be his anguish for the wickedness and the abominations of his people.
And he shall be called Jesus Christ, the Son of God,
and his mother shall be called Mary.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Both verses describe what shall happen; neither narrates the suffering as occurring in the present.
The supplied verses do not identify a speaker.
prohibited_inventions: Do not introduce King Benjamin or an angel.
Do not stage the foretold suffering as a present event or depict blood, wounds, or gore.
Do not invent an appearance for Jesus Christ or Mary.

title: Rejection, Crucifixion, and Resurrection Foretold
summary: The angel foretells that Jesus will be rejected, scourged, crucified, and rise on the third day, and that he will stand to judge the world.

explicit_facts.text: The angel foretells that Jesus will come unto his own, be considered a man and accused of having a devil, then scourged and crucified.
The angel foretells that Jesus will rise from the dead on the third day and stand to judge the world.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel is speaking to Benjamin in the remembered encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel’s appearance and all details of the future events.

spoken_dialogue.text: And he shall rise the third day from the dead;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: an angel from God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The events are foretold and must not be staged as present action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the scourging, crucifixion, resurrection, or judgment as happening in the angel’s scene.

title: Atonement and Repentance
summary: The angel teaches that Christ’s blood atones for certain people who have died without knowing God’s will or sinned ignorantly, and warns that those who knowingly rebel must repent and have faith in Jesus Christ for salvation.

explicit_facts.text: The angel says Christ’s blood atones for those who died not knowing God’s will or who sinned ignorantly.
The angel warns that salvation comes to one who knowingly rebels only through repentance and faith on the Lord Jesus Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel is speaking to Benjamin in the remembered encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel’s appearance and any visual representation of atonement or salvation.

spoken_dialogue.text: But wo, wo unto him who knoweth that he rebelleth against God!
spoken_dialogue.speaker: an angel from God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Teachings about atonement and salvation are not literal visual events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict symbolic blood, judgment, or afterlife scenes as literal events.

title: Prophets and the Law of Moses
summary: The angel teaches that prophets declared Christ’s coming so believers could receive remission of sins, and that God appointed the law of Moses for his stiffnecked people. Signs, wonders, types, shadows, and prophetic words pointed to Christ, but the people hardened their hearts and did not understand the law’s dependence on the atonement.

explicit_facts.text: The angel says the Lord sent holy prophets among all people to declare that Christ should come and that believers might receive remission of sins and rejoice.
The angel says God appointed the law of Moses to his stiffnecked people.

The angel says signs, wonders, types, shadows, and prophets showed the people Christ’s coming, but they hardened their hearts and did not understand that the law availed only through the atonement of Christ’s blood.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel is speaking to Benjamin in the remembered encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel’s appearance; the forms of the signs, wonders, types, and shadows.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The signs, types, and shadows are described as teachings and indications, not as specific visual events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent particular signs, wonders, prophets, or historical scenes.

title: Little Children and Salvation
summary: The angel teaches that little children are blessed and Christ’s blood atones for their sins, that salvation comes only through Christ, and that infants who die in infancy do not perish; people must humble themselves and believe in Christ’s atoning blood.

explicit_facts.text: The angel says little children are blessed and Christ’s blood atones for their sins.
The angel says salvation comes only through the name of Christ, the Lord Omnipotent.
The angel says an infant who dies in infancy does not perish and that people must humble themselves and believe in Christ’s atoning blood.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel is speaking to Benjamin in the remembered encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel’s appearance; whether any children are present in the remembered encounter.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses teach doctrine; they do not describe a child or infant physically present in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add children as visible characters or depict salvation as a visible supernatural event.

title: The Natural Man and the Holy Spirit
summary: The angel teaches that the natural man is an enemy to God unless he yields to the Holy Spirit, puts off the natural man through Christ’s atonement, and becomes childlike, submissive, meek, humble, patient, and loving.

explicit_facts.text: The angel teaches that the natural man is an enemy to God unless he yields to the Holy Spirit and becomes a saint through Christ’s atonement.
The angel describes becoming as a child: submissive, meek, humble, patient, full of love, and willing to submit to what the Lord sees fit.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel is speaking to Benjamin in the remembered encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel’s appearance; any visual form for the natural man or Holy Spirit.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The natural man and childlike qualities are figurative teachings, not characters or literal transformations.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a supernatural transformation or a personified natural man or Holy Spirit.

title: Knowledge of the Savior to Spread
summary: The angel foretells that knowledge of the Savior will spread among every nation, kindred, tongue, and people, and teaches that none will be blameless before God except little children, with repentance and faith in the Lord God Omnipotent.

explicit_facts.text: The angel foretells that knowledge of the Savior will spread throughout every nation, kindred, tongue, and people.
The angel teaches that none will be blameless before God except little children, and that repentance and faith are required.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel is speaking to Benjamin in the remembered encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel’s appearance and any future scenes of people receiving knowledge.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The spread of knowledge is future and not shown as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a montage of future nations or people.

title: The Speaker Concludes His Words
summary: A speaker tells an addressee that when the addressee has taught the people what the Lord commanded, they are found no more blameless in God's sight, only according to the speaker's words. The speaker says he has spoken the words the Lord God commanded him.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker addresses a person who is to teach their people the things the Lord their God commanded.
The speaker says that even then the people are found no more blameless in God's sight, only according to the words spoken to the addressee.
The speaker says he has spoken the words the Lord God commanded him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker addresses someone, but the verses do not establish what either person looks like.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's and addressee's identities and appearances.
The setting and whether the people mentioned are present.

spoken_dialogue.text: And even at this time, when thou shalt have taught thy people the things which the Lord thy God hath commanded thee, even then are they found no more blameless in the sight of God, only according to the words which I have spoken unto thee.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: And now I have spoken the words which the Lord God hath commanded me.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The teaching of the people is referred to in speech, not narrated as happening in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the speaker as an angel or the addressee as Benjamin from these verses alone.
Do not depict the teaching of the people or a departure as occurring here.

title: Testimony at the Judgment
summary: The Lord says that they will stand as a bright testimony against this people at judgment, when every person will be judged according to their works. Those whose works are evil will confront their guilt and shrink from the Lord’s presence into misery and endless torment.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says they will stand as a bright testimony against this people at the judgment day.
Every person will be judged according to their works, whether good or evil.
Those whose works are evil will face a view of their guilt and abominations and shrink from the Lord’s presence into misery and endless torment, from which they can no more return.

unspecified_visual_details: The physical setting and any visible appearance of the Lord or the people are not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: They shall stand as a bright testimony against this people, at the judgment day;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Judgment and its consequences are described as future events, not events occurring in a present setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord’s appearance or stage a present judgment or torment scene.
Do not identify what “they” refers to beyond the supplied verses.

title: The Cup of Wrath
summary: The angel says justice cannot deny the cup of God’s wrath to the wicked and mercy can no longer claim them; their torment is likened to an unquenchable lake of fire and brimstone. The angel says the Lord commanded him and ends with Amen.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says the wicked have drunk from the cup of God’s wrath, justice could not deny them, and mercy could claim them no more.
The Lord compares their torment to a lake of fire and brimstone with unquenchable flames and smoke ascending forever.
The angel says the Lord commanded him and concludes, Amen.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel is concluding his message to Benjamin.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel’s appearance and any literal setting for the figurative lake of fire and brimstone.

spoken_dialogue.text: Thus hath the Lord commanded me. Amen.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: an angel from God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The lake of fire and brimstone is presented as a comparison for torment; do not turn the figure of speech into a literal scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal lake of fire, visible flames, smoke, or damned people.
